measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: MIR-ATR immersion probe with a Zirconia or diamond ATR tip sealed in a PEEK shaft.
measurement_concept.location: In-line in the petroleum stream closer to the process.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: Chalcogenide (CIR) or polycrystalline infrared (PIR) fiber cables connecting the immersion probe to the spectrometer located outside the process area.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If water concentrations fall below detection limits or petroleum properties prevent ATR contact, alternative methods like NIR or laboratory cross-checks would be needed.
proposal.next_step: Conduct laboratory trials on representative petroleum samples using an MIR-ATR probe to establish calibration feasibility.

brief_answer: We recommend testing mid-infrared ATR spectroscopy first, as it is documented for water determination in petroleum streams. The analyzer can be placed outside the process area using fiber-optic links. Key unknowns such as stream optical regime, water concentration range, and process conditions must be clarified before finalizing equipment.
